output.Title: Path MTU Discovery

Publication.Publisher: RFC Editor, Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF)

output.Abstract: This document describes Path MTU Discovery, a mechanism for Internet hosts to determine the path maximum transmission unit (MTU) between themselves and any other host they wish to communicate with.

Sections.Title: Introduction
Sections.Content: Discusses the need for Path MTU Discovery, issues related to using fragmentation in data transmission, and references other relevant documents.

Sections.Title: Background
Sections.Content: Provides background on IP fragmentation, its limitations, and why discovering the Path MTU is necessary for efficient network communication.

Sections.Title: Path MTU Discovery Protocol
Sections.Content: Details the protocol implementation for Path MTU Discovery, including how hosts determine the Maximum Segment Size (MSS), the role of the 'Don't Fragment' bit, and handling of fragmentation errors.

Sections.Title: Plateau Table
Sections.Content: Presents a suggested table for common MTUs across various networks to facilitate Path MTU Discovery.

Sections.Title: Security Considerations
Sections.Content: Examines potential denial-of-service attacks that could exploit the Path MTU Discovery mechanism, recommending mitigation strategies.

Sections.Title: Implementation Notes
Sections.Content: Offers practical advice to implementors on efficiently managing and updating Path MTU estimates without requiring source code modifications.

Sections.Title: A Better Way to Detect PMTU Increases
Sections.Content: Suggests a refined approach for detecting increases in the Path Maximum Transmission Unit, optimizing for both efficiency and reduced resource waste.
